title: Role swap preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Alice's inputs drawn from a type $X$, Bob's from a type $Y$, and outputs in a type $\alpha$. Let $p^{\mathrm{swap}}$ be the protocol obtained by interchanging the roles of Alice and Bob throughout — turning every Alice node into a Bob node and vice versa while leaving output nodes unchanged. Then $p^{\mathrm{swap}}$ has the same communication complexity as $p$: the worst-case number of bits exchanged is unaffected by the swap.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic communication protocol over input types X (Alice) and Y (Bob) with outputs in α
replaced:
For any protocol $p$ over $X \times Y$,
\[
  p.\texttt{swap}.\texttt{complexity} \;=\; p.\texttt{complexity}.
\]
